title: Write clearly: briefs, updates and decision records
summary: Much of a PM's influence happens in writing. Clear, short documents help people understand quickly, decide well and remember why.

beginner: Start with the point: what you want the reader to know or decide.
Know your reader and what they already know.
Use short sentences, plain words and headings.
Cut anything that does not help the reader.
Ask a colleague to read it and tell you what they took away.
intermediate: Edit hard and test with a reader.
experienced: Write narratives that replace slide decks for big decisions.
Set writing standards for your team.
Use written decision records to build institutional memory.

toolExamples.google-docs: Use suggestion mode so reviewers propose cuts.
toolExamples.confluence: Use a decision record template: context, options, decision, reasons.
toolExamples.claude: Paste a draft and ask it to cut it by a third without losing meaning. Check the result.

definitionOfDone: Document leads with the main point
pitfalls: Writing for yourself, not the reader
